exposure: vascularization at cesarean scar on ultrasound
beta-human chorionic gonadotropin at hospital admission
outcome: treatment success of cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP)
cohort: The study included 161 women with cesarean scar pregnancies (CSPs) of 8 weeks or less, treated at TuDu Hospital between September 2017 and April 2019, divided into 63 failures (case group) and 98 successes (control group).
finding: COS-2 + on ultrasound significantly increased the likelihood of treatment success by 4.9 times, and other factors such as no vascularization at the cesarean scar, gestational mass volume ≤4 cm3, and β-human chorionic gonadotropin ≤ 10,000 mIU/mL also favored treatment success.
